items.title: Study outlines four options for saving Venice from rising seas

featured_image.name: MOSE flood barrier protects venice - see how it works

items.description:
A team of European researchers has laid out four possible futures for Venice — ranging from reinforcing its existing flood defenses to abandoning the city entirely — warning that without early action, the iconic UNESCO World Heritage Site could be lost within centuries.

The study, published Wednesday in the journal Scientific Reports, was led by oceanographer Piero Lionello of the University of Salento in Italy. It presents what the authors call an "adaptation pathways" framework, mapping out which strategies remain viable as sea levels climb under different emissions scenarios drawn from the IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report.[1][2]

items.title: Lebanon death toll reaches 2,196 as Israeli strikes continue

featured_image.name: Israeli raids displace a quarter of Lebanon's population

items.description:
Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health confirmed on Thursday that the cumulative death toll from Israeli military operations has risen to 2,196, with 7,185 others wounded since the conflict with Hezbollah erupted on March 2, according to the ministry's daily report from its Health Emergency Operations Center. In the past 24 hours alone, at least 29 people were killed and 124 wounded in strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon, Anadolu Agency reported.[1][2][3]

The escalating toll prompted Imran Riza, the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator for Lebanon, to warn that the human cost has "crossed a devastating threshold," noting more than 2,000 killed and 1.2 million displaced.[4]

items.title: China activates 60,000-chip AI science cluster built without US tech

featured_image.name: China activates largest scientific AI computing cluster in ...

items.description: China activated its largest artificial intelligence computing cluster for scientific research on Tuesday in Zhengzhou, central Henan province, doubling the facility's chip count from 30,000 to 60,000 domestically produced AI accelerators in just two months. The expansion, carried out entirely without American technology, marks a milestone in Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency in advanced computing amid tightening U.S. export controls.[1][2]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says
items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire set to take effect at 5 p.m. EST, pausing weeks of devastating Israeli strikes against Hezbollah that have killed more than 2,000 people in Lebanon since early March.

"These two Leaders have agreed that in order to achieve PEACE between their Countries, they will formally begin a 10 Day CEASEFIRE at 5 P.M. EST," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the agreement followed "excellent" conversations with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.[1][2][3]

Trump said he would invite both leaders to the White House for what he called "the first meaningful talks between Israel and Lebanon since 1983." He also said he had directed Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to work with both countries toward "a Lasting PEACE."[4][5][6]

items.title: Trump says Iran agreed to hand over enriched uranium as deal nears

featured_image.name: Iran war 'very close to over,' Trump says — and the stock market 'is going to boom'

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Thursday that Iran has agreed to relinquish its stockpile of enriched uranium, claiming the two sides are "close" to a peace deal to end over six weeks of war. The assertion came as Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian negotiators have scaled back ambitions for a comprehensive agreement and are instead pursuing a temporary memorandum to prevent a return to hostilities before the ceasefire expires on April 21.[1][2]

A separate source told Reuters that Iran had agreed to dilute its highly enriched uranium under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the United States. A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of parliament, said earlier this week that Tehran had agreed to dilute 450 kilograms of enriched uranium as a goodwill measure, though he added that the United States later backed out of that arrangement.[3][4][5]

items.title: White House clears path for federal agencies to use Anthropic's Mythos AI

featured_image.name: White House Moves to Give US Agencies Anthropic Mythos ...

items.description:
The White House Office of Management and Budget is establishing security protocols to allow major federal agencies to begin using Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, the powerful AI model that has rattled cybersecurity experts and financial regulators on both sides of the Atlantic since its limited release earlier this month. Federal CIO Gregory Barbaccia informed Cabinet departments of the plan, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg.[1]

The move comes even as government officials grapple with the model's potential to sharply increase cybersecurity risk — and despite an ongoing legal and political clash between the Trump administration and Anthropic over the use of the company's AI technology.

items.title: Pope Leo decries world 'ravaged by tyrants' amid feud with Trump

featured_image.name: Pope Leo decries world ravaged by 'tyrants' in speech ...

items.description: Pope Leo XIV delivered some of his most forceful remarks yet on Thursday, declaring that the world is "being ravaged by a handful of tyrants" during a peace gathering in the conflict-scarred city of Bamenda, Cameroon. The address, made at Saint Joseph Cathedral on the second day of his Cameroon visit, came amid an escalating public feud with U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the pontiff's opposition to the war in Iran.[1][2][3]
